chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever clothes his brother with a garment of winter or summer, it becomes a right upon Allah to clothe him from the garments of Paradise, and to ease upon him the pangs of death, and to expand for him in his grave, and that the Angels meet him when he exits from his grave with glad tidings.
And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'And the Angels will meet them: This is your Day which you were promised.'

key_terms.يُوَسِّعَ عَلَيْهِ فِي قَبْرِهِ: Expand for him in his grave

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for clothing a fellow Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing clothing a fellow believer as a specific act of *sadaqah* that triggers a multi-stage divine reward: from the ease of death (*sakarat al-mawt*) to the expansion of the grave (*was' al-qabr*). The Imam explicitly links this virtue to Surah Al-Anbiya 21:103, where angels greet the righteous with glad tidings, underscoring the continuity of mercy from the grave to the resurrection. This hadith is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence and ethics to encourage tangible, material charity among the *Mawma* beyond mere spiritual support.
